example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.o.name: Runbook
example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.o.body:
# When orders stop flowing

Check the **relay** first. See the [outbox pattern](https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html).

| signal | threshold | page |
|---|---|---|
| outbox rows | 10 000 | yes |
| relay lag | 60 s | no |

example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.p.name: Payment retry
example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.p.description: A flowchart, one of Payments' behaviours. It starts and ends at its marks; a decision's lines say where each answer goes.

example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.p.name: Incident summary
example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.p.body: Checkout was slow for twenty minutes while the card processor timed out. The breaker opened, the fallback queued charges, and every queued charge was taken once the processor came back.

example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.p.name: A retried checkout repeats the same key, so a retry never charges twice.

example.yaml.overview.shop.customer-faci.name: Storefront
example.yaml.overview.shop.customer-faci.description: An internal diagram: what the storefront is made of. Its pages meet through typed ports; its own ports sit on its walls.

example.yaml.overview.shop.data.1-model.name: Model
example.yaml.overview.shop.data.1-model.description: The records as classes — fields, then behaviours — joined by the associations stored between them, each end saying how many and in what role. Order status is a type, so it draws no card of its own.

example.yaml.overview.shop.data.2-schema.name: Schema
example.yaml.overview.shop.data.2-schema.description: The records as an entity relationship diagram — columns and keys — the same associations drawn as crow's feet.

example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.1.name: Checkout saga
example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.1.description: A sequence: who talks to whom, in what order. Each lifeline is a reference to the part it stands for, so it is the same Gateway, Storefront and Payments the shop is made of.

example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.2.name: Fulfilment
example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.2.description: A swimlane: who does what, in which phase. Each lane is a reference to the service that does the work; each phase a label on its row, which every step in it carries as a tag.

example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.2.name: Book carrier
example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.2.body: Shipping books a pickup in the carrier's terms.

example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.2.name: Pick items
example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.2.body: Stock is taken off the shelf.

example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.3.name: Deployment
example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.3.description: Where the shop runs. Groups nest: each a panel round its members, who carry it, with a note tied beside it; a grid lays environments under their headers: each environment a block of its own, each region a label on its row.

example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.4.name: Dashboard
example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.4.description: What the shop looks like from the operations floor: a picture card, drawn from its source.

services.yaml.patterns.anti-corruption-l.name: Anti-corruption layer
services.yaml.patterns.anti-corruption-l.body: Use when an outside system must be reached without its model leaking into ours.

services.yaml.patterns.anti-corruption-l.name: Keeps an outside model out of ours. Everything crossing is translated in one place.
Accepts a request already in our model.
Maps the outside model to ours and back.
The only part that speaks the outside protocol.

services.yaml.patterns.api-gateway.name: API gateway
services.yaml.patterns.api-gateway.body: Use when many clients reach many services and each request should be checked once, at one way in.

services.yaml.patterns.api-gateway:note-.name: One way in: every request is authenticated, held to its quota, then routed to the service that owns it.
Checks who is calling before anything else runs.
Turns away a caller over its quota.
Sends each request to the service that owns its path.

services.yaml.patterns.circuit-breaker.name: Circuit breaker
services.yaml.patterns.circuit-breaker.body: Use when a remote call can hang or fail, and a failing dependency must not take its callers down with it.

services.yaml.patterns.circuit-breaker:n.name: Calls pass while the remote answers. After repeated failures the breaker opens and the fallback answers until a trial call succeeds.
Counts failures. Closed, it passes calls; open, it fails fast.
Answers while the breaker is open.

services.yaml.patterns.layered-architect.name: Layered architecture
services.yaml.patterns.layered-architect.body: Use when one service owns its rules and its store, and every request should meet them in the same order.

services.yaml.patterns.layered-architect.name: Requests enter at the API, rules live in one layer, storage is reached only through the repository.
The only way in. It accepts the request and does no work of its own.
The rules live here, and nowhere else in the service.
Reads and writes the store; nothing else touches it.

services.yaml.patterns.saga-orchestrator.name: Saga orchestrator
services.yaml.patterns.saga-orchestrator.body: Use when one business action spans several services, each with its own store, and a failed step must undo the ones before it.

services.yaml.patterns.saga-orchestrator.name: The orchestrator sends each step's command in turn and records where it is. A failed step runs the compensations of the steps before it, newest first.
Where each running saga is, so a restart resumes it.

services.yaml.patterns.transactional-out.name: Transactional outbox
services.yaml.patterns.transactional-out.body: Use when a state change must announce itself, and neither the change nor the announcement may be lost.

services.yaml.patterns.transactional-out.name: A state change and the event announcing it are written in one transaction, so neither is lost.
Writes the state change and the event together.
The events, written beside the state they announce.
Reads the outbox and publishes each event at least once.
